translations.text: Now this holy father of ours, David, went away to desert and waterless places to judge himself, so that through a brief affliction he might gain that eternal and unending delight and rest.
For this reason he chose to judge himself here, outside, in the deserts. That is why that desert is called Garesja ("outer judgment").
He had with him one disciple, named Lucian. And when they reached that waterless desert,
they became very thirsty. They found a little rainwater collected in a cleft of the rock, drank from it, and sat down to rest in the shade of a rock.
And as they sat there, our holy father David said: "Brother Lucian, let us settle in this place and pray to God,
so that through quiet prayer, the shedding of tears and a little endurance, God may forgive our countless sins and offenses and grant us the delights and rest of the kingdom of heaven,
for affliction here is small and passing, but the glory there is unfailing and unending, and the glory is eternal. For this reason endurance is fitting here."
Lucian answered and said to him: "God-clothed father, truly it is so, as you say, and good things are given back to each person according to their deeds and labors.
But I see the great hardship and harshness of this desert, for it lacks everything needed: food and water.
And we are men living in the weakness of the flesh. How shall we bear the afflictions and trials of this desert?"

Our holy father David answered and said to him: "Brother Lucian, he who fed the people of Israel in the desert, made water spring up for them from hard rock, and rained quails on them in the midst of their camp,
and who fed Elijah by means of a raven, and gave food to holy Anthony and to the other holy fathers who dwelt in the mountains and deserts,
that same God is able now also to give us food to comfort the weakness of our flesh.
So now take courage, brother Lucian, and do not be afraid, for God is merciful and does not repay us according to our sins, but feeds with sweetness all who fear him."
Lucian was strengthened by these words and said to him: "As you command, holy father, so let us do everything."
They went about here and there and found a cave in the rock, and settled beneath it.
Whenever it was hot or it rained, they would rest under that cave. And they would gather food from the roots of meadow plants.
For it was springtime, and they found plenty of comfort for the body.
In this way they gathered food and glorified God, the giver of all good things.
After some days had passed, those meadow plants grew old and dried up from the heat, and their source of comfort failed. Lucian became distressed and said to holy David:
"Holy father, what will there be now to comfort the weakness of our flesh? For these meadow plants have dried up, from which we had hope of relief for our bodies."
Holy David answered and said to him: "Brother Lucian, do not set your hope on the meadow plants and the growth of the earth.
Do you not know that all earthly things are changeable and passing?
Have you not heard from the holy Scriptures: "By your endurance you will gain your souls"?
But you have quickly become faint-hearted. Do you not know that if we die of hunger or thirst for the sake of Christ's commandments, we are alive before God forever?
Yet you are greatly troubled and are wasting away over perishable food."
As he was saying this, three deer immediately came, followed by their fawns, and stood before them like tame sheep.
And father David said: "Lucian, brother, take a bowl and milk those deer."
He got up and milked them, and when he had filled the bowl, he brought it to the elder.
The elder made the sign of the cross over it, and it turned into curd cheese. They ate and were satisfied, and they glorified God.
And Lucian said to holy David: "Holy father, God is wonderful among his saints.
Now my heart has been strengthened and my soul is glad. From now on, even if my flesh decays and wastes away from hunger and thirst,
I will not worry at all about this mortal flesh and this vain transitory world."
And holy David said to him: "Blessed is God, who has strengthened your heart, and blessed is the holy name of his glory forever."
From then on the deer came every day except Wednesday and Friday, with their fawns accompanying them. In this way the two were refreshed in body and rejoiced in spirit.
Below the cave in which the saints lived there was another cave,
in which lived a great and terrifying dragon. It had blood-colored eyes, a horn on its forehead, and a thick mane [?] on its neck.
One day the deer passed by the entrance of that cave, and the dragon rushed at them, seized one fawn, and swallowed it.
The deer fled to the elder, frightened and trembling. When Lucian saw them trembling, he said to holy David:
"Holy father, these deer have come running in flight and are trembling terribly, and one fawn is not with them."
So David went out with a staff in his hands. When he went down to the place the deer had come up from, he saw the dragon and said to it:
"Evil dragon, why have you harmed our deer, whom God gave us as a comfort for the weakness of our flesh?
Now come out of that place and go away into the distant deserts. If you do not obey me,
by the power of our Lord Jesus Christ I will burst your belly with this staff of mine and make you food for worms."
But the dragon cried out: "Do not be angry, servant of God Most High. If you want me to leave this place, come up with me to the top of this mountain and be my guarantor,

so that you do not turn your eyes away from me until I go down into the water that flows on the south side of this mountain. For I am afraid of being struck by lightning, and that is why I cannot come out."
Holy David promised to do so, and the dragon came out. Holy David walked ahead of it, reciting the psalm:
"He who dwells in the help of the Most High shall rest in the shelter of the God of heaven."
As the dragon moved, the stones of that place shook. When Lucian saw this, he was afraid, fell on his face and lay there as if dead.
Holy David went up to the top of the mountain, and the dragon began to move even faster.
When it came out onto the plain of the desert, it went straight on, and the eyes of father David were turned toward it.
Then an angel of the Lord called out behind him and said to him, "David, David!"
He looked around, and as he turned, lightning struck the dragon and burned it up completely.
When holy David saw this, he was greatly distressed and said, "O Lord, King of glory,
why did you kill that dragon? It had put its hope and trust in me, and you have cruelly destroyed it."
Then the angel of God said to him, "Why are you grieving, you who are pleasing to our Lord Jesus Christ? If that dragon had gone down into the waters,
it would have gone from there into the seas, and there it would have grown very large by eating fish. It would have wrecked many ships in the seas and destroyed many souls in the waters.
So do not grieve over it, for this is what pleased the Lord.
Go now to your cave, for your disciple Lucian has fallen and lies on his face out of fear of the dragon.
Take him by the hand, raise him up, strengthen him and make him firm, and the two of you together glorify God, who has set you free from fear of that loathsome dragon."
At these words of the angel he came down from the mountain and found Lucian lying on the ground, frightened and trembling.
He took him by the hand, raised him up and said to him, "Brother Lucian, why were you afraid of a single worm, which God destroyed with fire in one moment?
Do not be afraid now, for the power of God is with us, and the grace of God protects all who fear him."
Lucian rejoiced at these words of the elder and gave thanks to the Lord.
Some days after this, some hunters came there from the region of Kakheti, for even to this day there is a great deal of game in those deserts:
deer and wild goats, and countless numbers of other wild animals of every kind. When the hunters arrived, they whistled to each other from one side and the other.
They saw the elder's deer going into the rock cave, and the hunters quickly went after them in order to trap them inside the rock cave.
When they reached the elder's cave, they saw the deer standing there while holy Lucian milked them.
When the men saw this they were struck with amazement. They ran and fell at the holy elder's feet and said to him, "How can this be, holy father,
that these deer, wild animals of the field, are so tame that they are gentler than sheep raised in the yards of houses?"
He said to them, "Why are you amazed at the mighty works of God? Have you not heard how Daniel tamed the lions, and how God kept the three young men unharmed by the fire?
So what is so wonderful about deer? But go and hunt other game, for the Lord has given these to us because of our weakness."
They said, "Great is the glory of the Lord! But make us worthy too of sharing in your holiness, holy father."
Their hearts were [?] moved, and they wept and said: "We will no longer return to our home. We will stay here with you, and from now on we will never leave you."
But he said to them: "Children and brothers, this place is harsh and difficult. Go back to your own dwellings."
With difficulty he somehow persuaded them to leave. When they had finished hunting, they went away and spread the news about him throughout the whole land.
People came running to the holy David from every direction. They begged him to let them live with him.
But he answered them: "Brothers, this place is harsh, and no comfort for the body is to be found in these parts."
They begged him and said: "Do not send us away, holy father. Even if we die here with you, we will not count it as death." When he could not persuade them otherwise, he said to them:
"Since you have placed your hope in God, go and get digging tools. Dig pits for water, and caves to live in as well."
They obeyed him and did as he commanded.
The brothers grew in number. When the holy and venerable father Dodo heard about him, he too came to father David, and they greeted one another.
A few days later, a great number of other brothers also gathered, and David said to father Dodo:
"Go, brother, to the ridge of this rock that stands opposite us, and take other brothers with you. They are eager to live apart and discipline themselves in the flesh for the life of their souls."
The holy Dodo obeyed his command. He went and built that desert monastery in the name of our all-holy Lady, the Mother of God,
and for the glory of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Day by day the number of brothers grew, and together they all glorified God.

Every day the holy father David would go out to the rock caves [?: "31" appears here in the text]. There, alone and in stillness, he performed his holy prayers, and he watered that desert with streams of sweat and tears.
One day, while he was praying like this, a certain barbarian by race from the region of Rustavi came there hunting game.
He set his hawk loose on a partridge near the place where the holy David was praying.
The partridge fled to the elder and settled at his feet, and the hawk landed near him.
This happened by God's providence, so that the hunter might himself be caught by His mercy.
The barbarian hurried over to take the partridge for his hawk.
He saw the saint standing in prayer and the partridge sitting at the saint's feet. The barbarian was amazed and said to him: "Where are you from?"
He answered in the Armenian language: "I am a sinful man, a servant of our Lord Jesus Christ. I am begging Him for His mercy,
so that He will forgive me all my sins and so that I may live out this brief life of mine in stillness and without disturbance."
The barbarian asked him again: "Who here feeds and comforts you?" He answered him: "The one in whom I hope and whom I worship,
He is the one who feeds and comforts all His creatures and everything He has made. By Him all people, all animals and all plants are fed,
the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea; and behold, this partridge too, fleeing in fear of your hawk, flees to me, the sinful servant of Christ.
So go away and hunt some other game, for today this one has taken refuge with me, so that it may be saved from death."
The barbarian answered him and said: "I want to kill you, so how can you save the partridge from death?"
But holy David said to him: "You have no power to kill me, nor this partridge either, for my Lord is with me, and he is the one who holds me by the hand [31]."
At these words of the elder, the barbarian, sitting on his horse, drew his sword to strike holy David.
But as he raised his hand, it withered at once and became like wood.
Then the barbarian understood his own wickedness. He got down from his horse, fell at the elder's feet, and begged him with tears to forgive his error.
Then holy David took pity on him and prayed to the Lord, saying: "Lord Jesus Christ, our God, who came for the salvation of the human race,
good and merciful one, who healed the withered hand: you yourself, O Master, [look on] this man who dared to raise his hand against your unworthy servant.
Let your grace and mercy come now as well, and heal this withered hand of the barbarian, so that he may understand and know you and glorify your name."
Then he put out his holy hand, and as soon as he touched it, it was healed at once by the help of God.
When the barbarian saw the majesty of God, he again began to plead with him with burning tears, and he said to holy David:
"Servant of the living God, in my house there is my son, who is lame in both feet and cannot stand up at all. Now I put my trust in your holiness
that you will pray to your Lord for him. If he is healed, His goodness will be glorified all the more, and I will bring the boy before your holiness so that you may bless him.
Then I and all my household will worship the name of Christ God. I will bring you abundant provisions, and you and all those with you will enjoy the produce of my house."
Holy David answered him and said: "Go to your home, and if God wills, you will find your son healed."
So he went to his home rejoicing, for he had also caught a great deal of game.
And when he reached his home — oh, your wonders, Christ!
For the lame boy, who used to crawl, came out joyfully to meet his father.
When his father saw that he was healthy and completely sound, he got down from his horse and gave thanks to God.
When he went into his halls, he asked his wife and household: "At what hour was this boy healed?"
They answered him and said: "Today at the third hour he got up and went about leaping like a gazelle."
Then he remembered that it was at that hour that the elder had said to him: "If God wills, your boy will be healed."
He told them everything that had happened to him and everything holy David had told him. And all of them together glorified God, our Lord Jesus Christ.
At dawn he loaded pack animals with abundant provisions: bread and wine, fish and many kinds of fruit, and he set off to Father David.
His son who had been healed came with him too, along with two other sons.
When they reached the place mentioned, and he did not see the elder, he was very upset and told a servant to look for him.
They went down to the lower part and found him with someone else. They came back and told him.
He went down to the elder with joy, fell at his holy feet, and said to him in tears:
"Truly I have found in you a healer of souls and bodies. Look, here standing before you is the boy who had no use of his feet, but today, through your prayers, he is healed and unharmed.
I have also brought these two other sons of mine before Your Holiness, so that they may touch your garment and be blessed by you."
He laid his holy hand on them and said: "May God, who blessed Jacob, in his goodness also bless you and make you children of the holy font."
After he had greeted them, Bubakr (for that was the name of this barbarian) ordered his servants to give the elder everything he had brought for him.
The elder gathered all the brothers, and they ate and drank and were satisfied.
When they rose from the meal, father David said to Bubakr: "What do you wish now, that we may do for you?" He begged him to baptize them.
He said to him: "Take some of your goods, go to father Dodo, and give them to him so that he can care for the brothers living there and give them rest, and you will be blessed by them.
He has with him an honourable priest, and I have sent word to him to send the priest along with you, and he will baptize you and all your household."
Then he sent holy Lucian with him and instructed him to tell Dodo to send a priest along to baptize Bubakr and all his household.
Holy Dodo did as the elder had ordered. When Bubakr had been baptized, this spiritual son by baptism came back again before holy David.
He brought diggers and workmen with him and built a church for him as a place of prayer for the brothers. Later the holy and God-clothed Hilarion enlarged this church and consecrated it.
On the south side of this church he made a beautiful shrine, in which the relics of our holy father David are buried.
To this day a fragrance rises from that tomb, and for all who take dust from that holy tomb with faith, it heals every human disease and infirmity.
The tomb of holy Lucian is directly in front of the altar.
He too is a helper, a comforter and a supporter for all who pray to them.
So much for this. But we were speaking about our holy and ever-memorable father David.
After some time had passed in this way and the number of brothers had grown, father David called Lucian and said to him:
"Brother Lucian, I am going to the holy city of Jerusalem. You lead these brothers whom we have gathered."
Lucian answered him: "If you go, I will come too, along with Your Holiness."
Holy David said to him: "No, brother, do not do this. It is not pleasing to God. If we do that and both go away, these brothers whom we have gathered
will scatter, each to the villages and cities. They will fall and perish through the desires of the sinful one, and God will hold us responsible for the ruin of their souls.
"But let me go alone, and I will entreat God for myself, for you and for these brothers who are with you. And do not think, brother, that I desire salvation for myself alone.
If I go, and God looks upon me with mercy, and through his goodness and sweetness lets fall upon me a drop of grace and sweetness,
may you and these brothers with you rejoice together with me. For I entreat God for all Christians together, and for all who dwell in this desert,
for mercy upon all, that he may make us worthy together of the eternal delights with all his saints."
With these and similar words he made Lucian stay with the brothers. He himself set out with a few other brothers and went to Jerusalem.
And when they reached the place called the Ridge of Thanksgiving, because holy Jerusalem comes into view from there, they raised their hands and offered thanks to God.
But the holy father fell down and soaked the ground with tears, and said: "O Lord God Jesus Christ,
who came to earth for the salvation of the human race, and in your goodness and mercy took upon yourself crucifixion and death for us sinners,
O Master, blessed, O Lord, is the holy name of your glory, for you have made even me, your unworthy servant, worthy to see these holy places.
But I no longer dare to go further and tread with my feet these places where your holy feet stood, for it is enough for me only to see them with my eyes."
And he wept and shed his holy tears.
And when his companions urged him to go on with them and enter Jerusalem, he answered and said to them:
"I no longer dare to go further. But you go, and pray for me, a sinner."
And when they had pressed him hard and he did not give in, they embraced him with tears, left him and went on.
When the holy David did this, God looked upon his holy mind and granted him grace beyond all who enter Jerusalem.
The holy David prayed earnestly to the Lord in that place. He picked up three stones from that place, put them in his bag as a blessing, and turned back from there.
That night God sent an angel to the Patriarch Elias, who said to him:
"My own servant David came as far as my house, and by his faith he has carried off the whole grace of Jerusalem.
Send swift runners after him at once, for he is going along the road to the city of Nablus.
He is dressed in old, tattered clothing, and an old bag hangs from him, in which he has put three stones that he took from the place
from which he turned back. Command those swift runners to take the stones out of the bag and give him back only one."
And [the angel told him to] say to him: "The Lord has granted you a third of the grace of Jerusalem, and he declares to you that by your faith you had carried off the grace of Jerusalem.
But I have chosen to have two parts returned, and the third I have granted to you.
Go and take it to your desert, sanctify the desert by your going there. Whoever comes to that desert and touches with faith the tomb of your bones
will receive healing of souls and bodies, and his sins will be forgiven him. And let that one stone be a memorial of this time."
When the angel of the Lord had told all this to the patriarch, he vanished from his sight.
At first the patriarch was astonished at the angel's words.
Then he fell on his face and offered a prayer to the Lord with tears. He summoned swift runners, told them all of this, and ordered them to bring him back. They too set off to overtake him.
They went, and when they caught up with him, they told him what the patriarch had ordered. They took the three stones from him and gave one of them back to him.
When holy David heard all this, he was at first shaken. Then he bowed down to the Lord and said with tears:
"Glory to you, Christ our God! And glory to you, holy Trinity, one Godhead, one essence!
Glory to you, God, who made us worthy to find mercy!" With words like these he offered thanks to the Lord.
The swift runners pressed holy David to return to Jerusalem, as the patriarch had ordered.
But he would not listen to them, so they kissed him and let him go.
When holy David reached his desert, all the brothers came out to meet him with joy. They glorified God, who had again shown them the shepherd and savior of their souls.
The brothers who had gone to Jerusalem with David finished their pilgrimage, and after this they too came to the desert of holy David.
They spread the story of him and of everything they had seen and heard concerning holy David.
A multitude of brothers gathered from every side, and the desert was filled. Some of them shut themselves away in clefts in the rocks.
Then the holy father and good shepherd, holy David, would go out day after day to visit the brothers who lived apart,
the recluses who lived alone. He comforted them all, strengthened and fortified them, and gave them the good news of the kingdom of heaven prepared for them.
Once he went to one of the brothers, who lived at the foot of a rock. He greeted him and said to him: "How are you, brother?"
He answered: "Well, through your holy prayers. But this water that drips from this rock is very bitter, and when I take some of it, it makes my senses bitter.
In the same way these herbs that are watered by it are also bitter, like gall. But I force myself and say:
'The torments of hell are far more bitter. Is it not better for you to endure for a single moment, so that you will not suffer that bitterness in hell for ever?'"
When he said this to holy David, David took pity on him and said to him:
"Do not be sad, brother. Let us pray to the Lord, and the gracious one who sweetened the waters at Marah will sweeten these as well."
They stood up and prayed to the Lord. Then David filled a vessel with the water, made the sign of the cross over it, and gave it to the monk.
When the monk tasted the water, it was sweeter than any other water. To this day that water is still sweet, and so are the herbs,
for since that time celery has grown in that place. Those who come to that place take some of the water and the herbs as a blessing (eulogia).
Such are the miracles that our father David performed, and he healed every human infirmity.
Also at the command of Father David, the desert monastery of Mravalmta was built in the name of Saint John the Baptist.
And after some time had passed in this place, Father David learned that he would soon depart from the body.
And he called all the brethren and said to them: "Brothers and spiritual children, see, I am departing from the body, like any other man."
"But do not be dismayed. Instead be steadfast and strong, and pray to God without ceasing for the salvation of your souls."

He ordered the priests to offer the sacrifice, and he received communion of the holy sacrifice of Christ God. Then he raised his hands and gave thanks to God, and so he committed his holy soul to the Lord.
And all the brethren wept at the loss of that good shepherd.
Among them was one of the brethren who had lost the sight of one eye. As soon as he touched that holy body he was healed at once, and everyone glorified God.
Such were the miracles the holy Father David worked even after his death. And so they buried him with honour in the coffin mentioned above.
And those who go to that tomb in faith receive healing of soul and body, and they glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
